prerequisites: Minimal familiarity as a common computer user

learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases, and computer programs with engineering applications.
Knowledge and use of programming fundamentals in telecommunications networks, systems, and services.
Locate computer science within engineering disciplines.
Understand the fundamentals of the binary system to comprehend information representation in computers.
Identify the hardware components that constitute a computer system, as well as their interconnection in networks, and understand their basic operation.
Distinguish the main peripherals used in a computer system and specifically in the field of engineering.
Classify the different types of software used in a computer system.
Identify and classify different types of computer systems and their application areas.
Understand the main functions performed by an operating system.
Analyze what services the operating system provides to programs and end-users.
Identify the main operating systems used in professional engineering environments and utilize their main services at a user level.
Understand the main functions performed by a database management system.
Create data models for simple problems.
Use basic expressions to retrieve and modify information stored in a database.
Identify which database management systems are used in professional engineering environments.
Identify the main application programs used in professional engineering environments.
Understand the concept of an algorithm and the process of abstracting a problem in programming.
Identify the program development process and its location within the general Software Engineering process.
Recognize the elementary data structures provided by a structured programming language.
Manage the elementary control structures of a structured programming language.
Abstract operations.
Design small applications to solve elementary problems in collaborative work environments.

syllabus_topics: INT - Introduction
Overview of computer science, in the context of other engineering disciplines
Structure and operation of a computer
Information representation in a computer
BD - Introduction to databases
Concept of database
Fundamentals of the relational data model
Performing queries and modifications
Database Management Systems in professional engineering environments
PRO - Introduction to programming
Problem abstraction for programming: fundamental concepts
Variables, expressions, assignment.
Using console input/output
Handling basic control flow structures: sequential, alternative, and repetitive
Definition and use of subprograms and functions. Scope of variables
File Input/Output
Basic data types and structures
Program development processes. From high-level to processor execution. Compiled languages and interpreted languages.
HSW - Hardware and software components of a computer system
Structure and operation of a computer: Von Neumann Architecture and machine language
Peripheral devices
System interconnection: types, mechanisms, and applications
Types of software: base software and application software
Types of computer systems and their application areas
SO - Introduction to operating systems
Concept and functions performed by an operating system
Interface and services offered to programs
Interface and services offered to users
Operating systems used in professional engineering environments
Introduction to tools in the practice laboratory. Spreadsheet as a tool (4h)
Design, implementation, and exploitation of a database (6h)
Programming with Python (18h)
Introduction to the development environment.
Variables, expressions, and console input-output.
Flow control: if-else, while, for.
Functions.
Structures: lists and strings.
Files.

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical exam (Theme 4 - Hardware and software components)
Theoretical exam (Theme 5 - Introduction to operating systems)
Practical exam (Theme 1 - Spreadsheet as a tool)
Practical exam (Theme 2 - Database design, implementation, and exploitation)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, to pass the theoretical block, at least 40% of the total score must be achieved in Theme 3 (Introduction to Programming), and a grade greater than 4 out of 10 for the theoretical block is required to average with the practical block. The final theoretical block grade is 'T'. To pass the practical block, at least 40% of the total score must be achieved in Theme 3 (P3), and a grade greater than 4 out of 10 for the practical block is required to average with the theoretical block. The final practical block grade is calculated as (0.15 * P1) + (0.20 * P2) + (0.65 * P3). If both minimums are met, the final grade is (0.5 * Theory) + (0.5 * Practices); otherwise, the grade is the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, the same conditions apply, but a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required for both theoretical and practical blocks to average, and prior grades of 5.0 or higher can be carried over. In case of doubt regarding authorship or unauthorized means, an in-person defense may be requested.
